This vignette demonstrates the enrichment analysis part of the `pecotmr`
package, which largely follows from `fastENLOC`
(https://github.com/xqwen/fastenloc) but uses `susieR` fitted objects as input
to estimate priors for use with the `coloc` package (coloc v5, aka
SuSiE-coloc). The main differences are:

1)  enrichment is based on all QTL variants whether or not they are inside
    signal clusters;
2) causal QTL are sampled from SuSiE single effects, not signal clusters;
3)  a variant may be a QTL for not only multiple conditions (e.g. cell types)
    but also multiple regions (e.g. genes).

The example uses de-identified data shipped with the package. All sample names,
variant positions, and identifiers are synthetic.

## Set up environment and load data

```{r load-pkgs}
library(pecotmr)
```

The enrichment pipeline consumes fine-mapping results as `pecotmr` S4 objects:
a `GwasFineMappingResult` for the GWAS and a `QtlFineMappingResult` for the
molecular QTLs. Both are shipped as example datasets.

```{r load-data}
data(gwasFineMappingExample)
data(qtlFineMappingExample)
gwasFineMappingExample
qtlFineMappingExample
```

## Input data

Each object is a `GRangesList`-backed collection, one element per tuple;
use the accessors rather than reaching into slots. `topLoci()` returns the
per-variant posterior summary as a `GRanges`, with the identity columns,
`pip`, and credible-set membership in `mcols()`:

```{r toploci}
head(topLoci(gwasFineMappingExample))
head(topLoci(qtlFineMappingExample))
```

Posterior inclusion probabilities across all variants in each region, taken
from the underlying SuSiE fit:

```{r pip-plots, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.2}
gwas_pip <- susieFit(gwasFineMappingExample)$pip
qtl_pip <- susieFit(qtlFineMappingExample)$pip
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(
    gwas_pip,
    ylab = "PIP",
    xlab = "Variant index",
    main = "GWAS PIPs",
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.6
)
plot(
    qtl_pip,
    ylab = "PIP",
    xlab = "Variant index",
    main = "QTL PIPs",
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.6
)
par(op)
```

## Perform enrichment analysis

`qtlEnrichmentPipeline()` takes the two fine-mapping collections directly and
estimates, for every combination of GWAS fit `(gwasStudy, gwasMethod)` and QTL
unit `(qtlStudy, qtlContext, qtlMethod)`, how enriched the molecular QTLs are
among the GWAS causal variants. Each fine-mapping method is its own fit: a
GWAS study fine-mapped with two methods gives two PIP vectors, never one. The
GWAS collection must be RSS-derived (every row carries an LD reference);
`gwasFineMappingExample` already does.

```{r enrichment}
enrich_res <- qtlEnrichmentPipeline(
    gwasFineMappingResult = gwasFineMappingExample,
    qtlFineMappingResult = qtlFineMappingExample,
    verbose = FALSE
)
enrich_res
```

The result is a data frame with one row per such combination, giving the
enrichment estimate (`enrichment`), its standard error (`enrichmentSe`), and
the log-odds (`enrichmentLogOdds`). These enrichment priors can then be
supplied to a colocalization analysis. This synthetic single-region example is
for illustration only; stable enrichment estimates require many fine-mapped
regions.

## The variant total

As in `fastENLOC`, both priors are PIP mass per variant: the GWAS prior is the
GWAS PIPs' sum, and the QTL prior the QTL fits' summed PIPs, over the total
number of variants the GWAS tested. QTL variants the GWAS PIP vector lacks take
part with GWAS PIP 0. A GWAS fine-mapping collection usually covers only its
fine-mapped blocks, far fewer variants than were tested, so pass that total as
`numGwas`, `fastENLOC`'s `-total_variants`. Without it the pipeline uses the
number of distinct variants in the two inputs and warns, as it did above;
that overstates both priors unless the GWAS PIPs are genome-wide.

```{r enrichment-num-gwas, eval = FALSE}
qtlEnrichmentPipeline(
    gwasFineMappingResult = gwasFmr,
    qtlFineMappingResult = qtlFmr,
    # e.g. the number of variants in the GWAS summary statistics
    qtlEnrichmentParam = QtlEnrichmentParam(numGwas = 12e6),
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(8),
    seed = 1
)
```
